Verify user exists and belongs to the tenant\n74\t   * 2. Revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens\n75\t   * 3. Anonymize PII fields (email, password — makes account irrecoverable)\n76\t   */\n77\t  async executeErasure(\n78\t    userId: string,\n79\t    tenantId: string,\n80\t    requestedBy: string,\n81\t  ): Promise<void> {\n82\t    this.logger.log(`GDPR erasure initiated: userId=${userId} requestedBy=${requestedBy}`);\n83\t\n84\t    const user = await this.userRepository.findOne({\n85\t      where: { id: userId, tenantId },\n86\t    });\n87\t\n88\t    if (!user) {\n89\t      throw new NotFoundException(`User ${userId} not found in tenant ${tenantId}`);\n90\t    }\n91\t\n92\t    // LEGAL-HIGH-005 cure: BEFORE any destructive op, consult the\n93\t    // canonical legal-hold registry. A tenant-wide hold blocks ALL\n94\t    // erasure under that tenant; a user-scoped hold blocks just this\n95\t    // user. If the legal-hold infrastructure isn't wired (local-dev\n96\t    // path), the optional dependency is undefined and the check is\n97\t    // skipped — production has the module registered and the assert\n98\t    // throws LegalHoldActiveError on hit.\n99\t    if (this.legalHoldService) {\n100\t      await this.legalHoldService.assertNoHold(tenantId, 'tenant');\n101\t      await this.legalHoldService.assertNoHold(tenantId, 'user', userId);\n102\t    }\n103\t\n104\t    // Revoke all sessions and tokens first — prevents further authentication\n105\t    // with any existing credentials while erasure is in progress.\n106\t    await this.authService.logoutAllDevices(userId);\n107\t\n108\t    // M-GDPR-03: Delete WebAuthn credentials (passkeys/security keys).\n109\t    // credentialPublicKey is linked to a physical device owned by the user —\n110\t    // constitutes personal data under strict GDPR interpretation.\n111\t    await this.webAuthnService.removeAllCredentials(userId);\n112\t\n113\t    // Anonymize PII fields and lock account in one transaction.\n114\t    // Email is replaced with a non-reversible placeholder that preserves\n115\t    // uniqueness (userId-scoped) so the DB unique constraint is not violated.\n116\t    // WHY placeholder format: some services hold email as a FK-like reference;\n117\t    // 'deleted-{userId}@gdpr.local' preserves referential integrity while\n118\t    // making the original email unrecoverable.\n119\t    await this.dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => {\n120\t      // User entity has no updatedBy field — requestedBy is logged above for audit trail.\n121\t      await manager.update(User, { id: userId }, {\n122\t        email: `deleted-${userId}@gdpr.local`,\n123\t        password: '',\n124\t        isActive: false,\n125\t      });\n126\t\n127\t      // Belt-and-suspenders: ensure all refresh tokens are revoked even if\n128\t      // logoutAllDevices() missed any due to a race condition.\n129\t      await manager.update(\n130\t        RefreshToken,\n131\t        { userId, isRevoked: false },\n132\t        { isRevoked: true, revokedAt: new Date(), revokedReason: 'GDPR erasure' },\n133\t      );\n134\t\n135\t      // M-GDPR-01 + DATA-HIGH-001: the UserDeleted event is the ONLY trigger\n136\t      // for cross-service GDPR cleanup (messaging/hr/farm/sensor) — without it,\n137\t      // only auth-layer PII is erased and personal data lingers downstream.\n138\t      // Enqueue it in the SAME transaction as the anonymisation so the event\n139\t      // and the erasure commit atomically (no dual-write loss); the outbox\n140\t      // worker then publishes to NATS at-least-once. tenantId is the validated\n141\t      // erasure tenant (a UUID), which the outbox requires.\n142\t      await this.outboxPublisher.enqueue(\n143\t        {\n144\t          ...createBaseEvent('UserDeleted', tenantId, { userId: requestedBy }),\n145\t          deletedUserId: userId,\n146\t          tenantId,\n147\t          erasureType: 'gdpr_right_to_erasure',\n148\t        },\n149\t        manager,"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8d9b98be-cb57-44b7-8fbe-049dd56dcb55","uuid":"e0a6c674-379a-496a-b039-c803a10f05e7","timestamp":"2026-10-08T09:03:25.706Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/gharunner/actions-runner/_work/aquaculture_platform/aquaculture_platform/aria-worktrees/req-AIR-aria-evidence-judge-3aa603f966aa/apps/auth-service/src/privacy/gdpr-compliance.service.ts","content":" Verify user exists and belongs to the tenant\n   * 2. Revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens\n   * 3. Anonymize PII fields (email, password — makes account irrecoverable)\n   */\n  async executeErasure(\n    userId: string,\n    tenantId: string,\n    requestedBy: string,\n  ): Promise<void> {\n    this.logger.log(`GDPR erasure initiated: userId=${userId} requestedBy=${requestedBy}`);\n\n    const user = await this.userRepository.findOne({\n      where: { id: userId, tenantId },\n    });\n\n    if (!user) {\n      throw new NotFoundException(`User ${userId} not found in tenant ${tenantId}`);\n    }\n\n    // LEGAL-HIGH-005 cure: BEFORE any destructive op, consult the\n    // canonical legal-hold registry. A tenant-wide hold blocks ALL\n    // erasure under that tenant; a user-scoped hold blocks just this\n    // user. If the legal-hold infrastructure isn't wired (local-dev\n    // path), the optional dependency is undefined and the check is\n    // skipped — production has the module registered and the assert\n    // throws LegalHoldActiveError on hit.\n    if (this.legalHoldService) {\n      await this.legalHoldService.assertNoHold(tenantId, 'tenant');\n      await this.legalHoldService.assertNoHold(tenantId, 'user', userId);\n    }\n\n    // Revoke all sessions and tokens first — prevents further authentication\n    // with any existing credentials while erasure is in progress.\n    await this.authService.logoutAllDevices(userId);\n\n    // M-GDPR-03: Delete WebAuthn credentials (passkeys/security keys).\n    // credentialPublicKey is linked to a physical device owned by the user —\n    // constitutes personal data under strict GDPR interpretation.\n    await this.webAuthnService.removeAllCredentials(userId);\n\n    // Anonymize PII fields and lock account in one transaction.\n    // Email is replaced with a non-reversible placeholder that preserves\n    // uniqueness (userId-scoped) so the DB unique constraint is not violated.\n    // WHY placeholder format: some services hold email as a FK-like reference;\n    // 'deleted-{userId}@gdpr.local' preserves referential integrity while\n    // making the original email unrecoverable.\n    await this.dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => {\n      // User entity has no updatedBy field — requestedBy is logged above for audit trail.\n      await manager.update(User, { id: userId }, {\n        email: `deleted-${userId}@gdpr.local`,\n        password: '',\n        isActive: false,\n      });\n\n      // Belt-and-suspenders: ensure all refresh tokens are revoked even if\n      // logoutAllDevices() missed any due to a race condition.\n      await manager.update(\n        RefreshToken,\n        { userId, isRevoked: false },\n        { isRevoked: true, revokedAt: new Date(), revokedReason: 'GDPR erasure' },\n      );\n\n      // M-GDPR-01 + DATA-HIGH-001: the UserDeleted event is the ONLY trigger\n      // for cross-service GDPR cleanup (messaging/hr/farm/sensor) — without it,\n      // only auth-layer PII is erased and personal data lingers downstream.\n      // Enqueue it in the SAME transaction as the anonymisation so the event\n      // and the erasure commit atomically (no dual-write loss); the outbox\n      // worker then publishes to NATS at-least-once. tenantId is the validated\n      // erasure tenant (a UUID), which the outbox requires.\n      await this.outboxPublisher.enqueue(\n        {\n          ...createBaseEvent('UserDeleted', tenantId, { userId: requestedBy }),\n          deletedUserId: userId,\n          tenantId,\n          erasureType: 'gdpr_right_to_erasure',\n        },\n        manager,","numLines":90,"startLine":60,"totalLines":195}}}
